content: The protein known as DCC1, or sister chromatid cohesion protein DCC1, is encoded in humans by the DSCC1 gene. Model organisms have been utilized to investigate the function of DSCC1. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Dscc1tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was developed at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a high-throughput mutagenesis initiative designed to create and distribute animal models of human diseases to researchers. Both male and female mice underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of DSCC1 gene deletion. A total of 24 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, and four significant abnormalities were identified. During gestation, very few homozygous mutant embryos were detected, and some exhibited edema. Consequently, fewer embryos than expected survived to the weaning stage. Among those that did survive, increased chromosomal instability was observed in a micronucleus test, and numerous skeletal abnormalities were identified through radiographic analysis. Additionally, DCC1 has been demonstrated to interact with the protein CHTF18.
